heroHeadline: Sittwe Front Reignites After Month-Long Lull as Min Aung Hlaing Lands in Hanoi for Fourth ASEAN Visit; AAPP Toll Passes 8,335 — Day 2,044
heroSubtitle: On Day 2,044 (September 7, 2026), Myanmar's civil war shows the same split-screen pattern of combat and diplomacy. On September 4, fighting resumed along the Sittwe-Ponnagyun border after a roughly month-long lull, with the junta and Arakan Army trading heavy artillery, MLRS and drone strikes that displaced thousands from Ponnagyun and Rathedaung townships and damaged a 450-year-old pagoda for the third time. The same day, President Min Aung Hlaing landed in Hanoi for a three-day state visit — his fourth ASEAN stop since becoming civilian president in April, disclosing that Myanmar-Vietnam trade has collapsed from $853M in 2020 to just $335M in the first half of 2026; a Cambodia visit follows September 11-12. In the north, the junta's battered Ayeyarwady River flotilla — which lost 8 of 15 vessels and over 100 personnel captured or surrendered to a KIA-PDF ambush near Zinbon on September 2 — limped into Bhamo on September 3, and the regime struck back on September 6 with an airstrike damaging the KIA-held Sinkhan Bridge crossing. Junta airstrikes also killed 5 civilians in Mawchi's tungsten-mining district (Sept 1), 9 more across two Karenni villages along the Loikaw-Shadaw road (Sept 5), and 2 in a Minbu Township raid (Sept 5), while resistance forces captured a Light Infantry Battalion position near Loi Htwe (Sept 2) and mined a junta convoy near Natmauk (Sept 6). AAPP's September 7 tally puts confirmed deaths since the 2021 coup at 8,335, with 31,887 people arrested and 22,663 still detained or unverified; ACLED separately confirmed in July that cumulative conflict deaths across all actors have surpassed 100,000. IDPs remain at approximately 5.2 million, with only 26% of the 2025 UN humanitarian appeal funded.
